headline: Mother's phone recovered from suspect's house in Cumilla teen murder case
summary: Police have recovered the iPhone of 13-year-old Ishiat Shahriar Opratim's mother from a suspect's house. Opratim was found dead near Comilla University after going missing with the phone.
details: Police have recovered the iPhone belonging to the mother of 13-year-old Ishiat Shahriar Opratim, who was found dead near Comilla University. The phone was found at the house of a suspect named Tuhin.

Opratim, a Class VII student, left home on Friday afternoon, telling his parents he was going out to take photographs with his mother’s iPhone. His body was recovered from the Sananda hillocks on the outskirts of Cumilla on Saturday afternoon, nearly 24 hours after he went missing.

The victim was the only son of Nahida Begum, an associate professor at Comilla University, and businessman KM Firoz Shahriar. Three young men, identified as Tuhin, Anas, and Fahim, aged between 18 and 20, have been detained in connection with the alleged killing.
Police are currently analyzing CCTV footage and questioning the suspects. Cumilla Superintendent of Police Anisuzzaman is scheduled to brief the media about the ongoing investigation today (Sunday).
No case had been filed until 9:00 PM on Saturday, according to Md Rakibul Hasan, officer-in-charge of Cumilla Sadar South Police Station.

headline_marked: [[Iran sends conditions to US via Qatar]] to end war, return to talks
headline: Iran sends conditions to US via Qatar to end war, return to talks
summary: Iran's top security official, Mohsen Rezaei, confirmed sending formal conditions to Washington through Qatar, including ending the war, releasing frozen funds, and lifting the naval blockade. Tehran awaits a response from President Trump.
details: Iran has formally sent conditions to the United States via Qatar to end the ongoing war. Mohsen Rezaei, a top security official, confirmed this to Al Jazeera, stating they are awaiting President Trump's response.

The conditions include ending the war on all fronts, releasing frozen Iranian funds, and lifting the naval blockade. Rezaei emphasized that accepting these terms is in Washington's interest, dismissing Trump's threats.

The conflict began after a joint US-Israeli attack in Iran in late February, which killed Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. Qatar and Pakistan have been working to bring both nations back to the negotiating table since their previous Memorandum of Understanding expired last month.

Rezaei did not rule out the possibility of new US attacks, citing strong military assessments, but assured Tehran is fully prepared. He mentioned Iran has altered its military plans, now focusing on the US Navy from the Persian Gulf to the Arabian Sea.

Iran recently conducted successful tests of ship-destroying missiles with multiple warheads near US warships, with plans for future enhancements. Rezaei warned that any future Iranian counter-attack would be more intense, targeting US military bases, commercial interests, and companies in the region.

David Des Roches, former director for the Arabian Peninsula at the Pentagon, told Al Jazeera that Washington might not view these conditions as a serious start to negotiations, possibly seeing it as a form of Iranian surrender. However, he noted Iran's shift from its previous demand for war compensation.
